reason: The cited evidence shows that WC additions (5–60 wt%) to various HEA coatings improve hardness and wear resistance, but it does not support the specific claim that 0.2–0.3 wt% WC is sufficient for a 30–50% improvement, nor does it address coating Ti-6Al-4V with AlCoCrFeNi-WC or performance at elevated temperatures. Evidence E2 and E4 highlight common issues with cracking and uneven WC distribution, which contradicts the premise of a defect-free, uniform coating.
premises: Laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi with WC particles can produce a metallurgically bonded, dual-phase coating on Ti alloys.
Adding WC particles to HEA coatings increases microhardness and wear resistance.
A WC content of 0.2–0.3 wt% is sufficient to achieve a 30–50% improvement in hardness and wear resistance.
The coating will have a uniform dispersion of WC particles without defects like cracks or delamination.
The improvements will be maintained under dry sliding wear at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
